section.computation: synthesis of the corrected record; number lint

ledger.input: first run behavioral analysis (similar to repo mentioned above)
ledger.output: Qwen3-8B writes BFS and Dijkstra almost without exception on the two path search tasks and one algorithm on each of 13 further coding tasks (modal share 1.00 on 12, 0.98 on one); the collapse is not universal: three of 15 new tasks are already mixed in the instruct twin.
ledger.metadata_sources: Sections 1.4, 5.4, 5.5 and 'What we have learned so far'

ledger.input: implement path saerch algorithm -> does llm always design BFS?
ledger.output: Mostly BFS or DFS on the grid task: Qwen3-8B and eight more open configurations write BFS or DFS at baseline, apart from a few programs labelled other or invalid; Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct's correct grid programs are BFS 20 of 20, gemma-3-4b-it writes DFS in about 70% and BFS in about 30% for one grid prompt, and gpt-oss-120b writes BFS 45 and DFS 5 of 50; on weighted shortest path the default is Dijkstra.

ledger.input: 1 a) does a tight temp, with topk=10 produce 10 reasoning trajectories of 1 idea/solution but same 10 phrasings
ledger.output: Closest to (a): at tight temperature a model has few ideas, often one, in proportions its fork logits fix, and many phrasings of each; iterations 1 to 4 changed the algorithm in 0 of 20 seeds under a shared seed while phrasings multiplied.

ledger.input: 1 b) or does tight temp, with topk=10 produce 10 reasoning trajectories of 10 ideas/solutions with 1 phrasing each
ledger.output: No: trajectories do not spread over ten ideas; the algorithm is decided at one or two fork tokens whose entropy given the fork token's class is at most 0.19 bits, and on the collapsed tasks fork margins of 4.85 to 17.04 nats put the alternative out of reach.

ledger.input: c) and does loosing up temp, make a) more to 2/3/4 ideas each with 10 phrasings ; or make b) keep original 10 ideas, now each with 10 phrasings
ledger.output: Loosening temperature reweights the ideas the fork already weighs, as a law composed over the forks predicts (mean total variation 0.029 to 0.054 on three Qwen3-8B units), with more phrasings of each as T rises; it does not add ideas on collapsed tasks (connected components reaches DFS in at most 18% of programs).

ledger.input: (always same seed)
ledger.output: The test under the same seed was run with thinking on and off and with top-k 10, and later arms share common random numbers, so every contrast is paired on the same draws.

ledger.input: top-k 10
ledger.output: top-k 10 gives the same programs as top-p 1 because every fork token lies in the top 10.
ledger.metadata_sources: Sections 7.5, 'What we have learned so far'

ledger.input: 2 can context seeding help? prepand "seed=d32qxk4nt43" or "seed=(horse chair roof love)"
ledger.output: No change of algorithm: under the entropy seed the grid task stays BFS 100 and shortest path Dijkstra 100, and in Qwen3-8B's later cell list both random seeds give Dijkstra 30 of 30 programs; the entropy seed stays within the paraphrase noise of the read-position state (0.734 and 1.165; on shortest path its 90% interval reaches 1.596, so equivalence was not shown there), and the word seed moves the grid state 1.555 times the noise without changing the program.

ledger.input: 3 so how much does prompt instructions matter? ("Make a new algorithm", "Make a fully novel algorithm never seen before ... 2000 words ...")
ledger.output: The long-form novelty instructions (about 2,000 words of design rationale before the code) produce claims of novelty, not new algorithms: of 574 outputs with a claim record, 484 (84%) claimed a new algorithm, and 220 of the 295 with code (75%) were catalogue algorithms; on shortest path the 2,000-word instruction gives Dijkstra 22 and Bellman-Ford/SPFA 6 correct programs of 30 in Qwen3-8B.

ledger.input: hyp: is llm a probablistic model, and thus gives you the average/mean answer? and only context pushes you into a different subspace
ledger.output: The instruct default is a sharpened choice of the base model, not its mean answer: on the three collapsed Qwen3-8B tasks the instruct fork margin exceeds the base model's by 2.1 to 13.4 nats while phrasing entropy moves by under 0.5 nats; in Gemma the grid fork gains 1.78 nats and post-training reversed and concentrated the base model's preference (base P(BFS) 0.25, 0.663 of base mass unmapped).

ledger.input: analyze the internals , all the runs that produced BFS , vs all runs that produced DFS , vs dijkstra
ledger.output: Natural BFS against DFS internals were read within a ban in Qwen3-8B and within one prompt in Gemma, with circuits for the fork in both; the algorithm is decided at the fork, and the fork log-odds is linearly decodable from Gemma's residual stream there (R-squared 0.66 on SAE codes against 0.18 for text).

ledger.input: analyze with thought anchors
ledger.output: Thought anchors and forks were run: the decisive position is one or two generated tokens after a shared opening of 18 to 61 tokens, the fork.

ledger.input: NLA
ledger.output: A natural language autoencoder on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct names the algorithm only where the prompt names it, and an outside reader of the visible text predicts it better.

ledger.input: SAE
ledger.output: Gemma Scope 2 features read Gemma's fork (R-squared 0.66 against 0.18 for text) but steer it less than a difference-in-means direction, which moves the fork 2.3 times as far as the SAE clamp at matched norm.

ledger.input: logit lens / j-lens
ledger.output: The logit and tuned lenses found no veto layer at the commitment token, because the fork has already happened at the first token; the community Jacobian lens for Qwen3-8B agreed with the next token less than the logit lens at every layer (0.104 against 0.291 at layer 27).

ledger.input: circuits
ledger.output: Path-patching circuits for the fork margin show a late stack of fork-position MLPs and heads carrying the fork logit in both families, but specificity fails at those sites under steering, DAS and cross-model patching; most matched random patching sets repeat a component, and the repaired layer-0 condition MLP gives about 7.9 nats on the five forced held-out prompts and about 0 on the five padded twins.

ledger.input: plot a "path search algorithm" manifold, color each algorithm centroid by implemented-count (geodesic and mds; actual activation space)
ledger.output: Geometry plots in actual activation coordinates exist from iterations 2 to 9, using geodesic distances, Isomap, MDS and centroids sized by implemented count, including four manifolds of the ten algorithms built with and without names in two models (iteration 9).

ledger.input: then prohibit the top 5 in prompt, and see if the implemented count moves to the edge of those 5, or to the opposite side
ledger.output: It depends on the map: unit-weight Dijkstra lies opposite the banned five on every manifold built from language (g 1.63, 1.20 and 1.08 times the median) and at the edge on the program manifold (0.67); its survivors place at the edge (15 of 15 on the primary frames, 10 of 15 on the programs-only frame) and the 15 Bellman-Ford/SPFA survivors opposite on both gate-passing Qwen3-32B frames. By mechanism the obeying model's survivors are mostly not renamed BFS by hand reads (0.30 unit-weight Dijkstra), and the exhaustion gap depends on the reading (Qwen3-32B by hand reads 0.30, by the runtime label 0.67).
ledger.metadata_open_in: TP-G2 (preregistered placements); NOV-R (single-instrument retest of the described ban)

ledger.input: (if its a circle manifold)
ledger.output: No loop at the label-dependent position; persistent loops exceed their coordinate-permutation null only on the shortest path task at block 18 and two sum at blocks 18 and 23, and a planted circle at matched size and noise was detected in every case.

ledger.input: can we make llms give truly creative and novel solutions?
ledger.output: No intervention so far produced a correct novel algorithm: none of 568 correct programs under bans and none of 237 after fork interventions in iteration 9; the evaluator-guided search on a scored task, whose bin-packing harness passed its gate before the workspace was lost, is the route not yet run.
ledger.metadata_sources: Sections 9.3, 9.6, 9.9; 'What we have learned so far'
ledger.metadata_open_in: NOV-B1/B2 (bin packing, evaluator-guided search); NOV-T (TSP replication)

ledger.input: is "temp" really the "llm creativity knob"?
ledger.output: No: temperature acts on the algorithm only through one or two fork tokens and reweights ideas the fork already weighs; where the fork margin is 4.85 to 17.04 nats the alternative stays out of reach, and lowering T from 1.0 to 0.3 moves the output toward the default.
